title: Subsets II
corePattern: Backtracking with Sorting and Duplicate Skipping
interviewTips: Ask if output order matters and if empty subset should be included - yes for this problem.
Trade-off: bitmask plus set is simplest to code but has hashing overhead; sorted backtracking avoids duplicates without extra set and is expected optimal.
Edge-case tip: sort first so duplicates are adjacent, and only skip duplicates at the same recursion level with condition i > start.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force Bitmask plus Deduplication
approaches.intuition: Every subset corresponds to a binary mask of length n. Enumerate all 2^n masks, build the subset, and deduplicate with a hash set.
approaches.theory: Sort nums so equal values produce identical ordered tuples. For each mask from 0 to 2^n - 1, collect nums[i] where bit i is set. Use a set of tuples or vectors to keep only first occurrence of each distinct subset. Sorting gives canonical form so duplicates map to same key.

timeComplexity.explanation: Sort O(n log n) plus 2^n masks each building subset in O(n) and set insert O(n) for hashing or comparison, dominated by O(n * 2^n).

spaceComplexity.explanation: Output holds up to 2^n subsets of average length n/2, plus set of same order in worst case with all distinct elements.

steps: mask 4 -> [2], duplicate of mask 2, skipped by set

edgeCases: All duplicates e.g. [2,2,2] -> only n+1 subsets
All distinct e.g. [1,2,3] -> full 2^n subsets, set never hits

approaches.name: Approach 2: Sorted Backtracking with Duplicate Skip
approaches.intuition: Sort so duplicates are adjacent, then do DFS that appends current path as a valid subset. At each level skip a duplicate value if it was not chosen as the first occurrence at that level.
approaches.theory: This is include-or-exclude decision tree with pruning. After sorting, equal values are contiguous. Loop i from start to n-1: if i > start and nums[i]==nums[i-1], skipping avoids generating same subset twice from same level while still allowing [2,2] via deeper recursion. Each distinct subset is generated exactly once, no set needed. Correctness follows by grouping subsets by first differing position.

timeComplexity.explanation: Sorting O(n log n). In worst case number of distinct subsets is 2^n and copying each path costs O(n). No set overhead, optimal for enumeration.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Recursion depth and path use O(n) auxiliary space excluding output. Output itself is O(n * 2^n) which is required.

steps: from [1]: i=1 pick 2 -> [1,2], then recurse adds [1,2,2]; i=2 is duplicate at same level (i>start) so skipped
back to root: i=1 pick 2 -> [2], recurse adds [2,2]
root i=2 skipped because nums[2]==nums[1] and i>start

edgeCases: Negative numbers and zeros - sorting still works

approaches.name: Approach 3: Iterative Expansion with Previous Size
approaches.intuition: Build subsets incrementally. When current number is new, extend all existing subsets. When it is duplicate, only extend subsets created in previous step to avoid duplicates.
approaches.theory: Let res hold all distinct subsets of prefix. For nums[i], new subsets are {s U {nums[i]} for s in res}. If nums[i] != nums[i-1], s ranges over all of res. If duplicate, any s not containing previous duplicate would duplicate work already done, so restrict s to those added in last iteration (from index prevSize to size-1). Tracking prevSize gives exactly the needed range. Sorting ensures duplicates are consecutive.

timeComplexity.explanation: Each of up to 2^n subsets is created once by copying list of length up to n. Sorting O(n log n) is negligible.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Stores all subsets in res. Only O(1) extra variables prevSize, size, start besides output.

steps: i=0 val 1 distinct: start 0, size 1, add [1] -> res=[[],[1]], prevSize=1
i=1 val 2 distinct: start 0, size 2, add [2],[1,2] -> res=[[],[1],[2],[1,2]], prevSize=2
i=2 val 2 duplicate: start=prevSize=2, size 4, only extend res[2]=[2] and res[3]=[1,2] -> add [2,2],[1,2,2]

edgeCases: Long run of duplicates [0,0,0,0] -> start restricts correctly each time
Mixed duplicates [4,4,4,1,4] -> sorting to [1,4,4,4,4] essential before iteration
